title: RE: IP-1 Staging and Access — Confirm by 10:00

fields.to: IP-1 Quarantine Officer, Minnesota Board of Animal Health; eoc.ops@caldercountymn.example
fields.subject: RE: IP-1 — staging and access CONFIRM BY 10:00
fields.body:
Answering (2) for roads. EOC will need to answer (1).

The CR 12 bridge, 0.4 mi east of the main drive, is still posted 10 tons. A loaded rendering truck or a lowboy carrying depop equipment can't legally cross it. The 230th Street field lane to the north service gate is the only route those trucks have. If the order lists just the CR 12 drive, the heavy trucks will have no legal way in.

I can have Type III barricades at the 230th lane entrance by 10:30. Before my crew sets them, I need someone to tell me whether this is a controlled gate, with permitted trucks passing through and someone logging them, or a closure. If it's a gate, it needs someone standing at it. A barricade can't check a permit.

Sketch of the lane and gate attached.

-----Original Message-----
From: IP-1 Quarantine Officer, Minnesota Board of Animal Health
Sent: Tue 10/20/2026 9:10 AM
To: eoc.ops@caldercountymn.example
Cc: highway@caldercountymn.example
Subject: IP-1 — staging and access CONFIRM BY 10:00

(1) Please confirm the Calder County Fairgrounds west lot as staging for PPE, vehicles and crews. The state hand-wash and shower trailers are dispatched and arrive within 12 hours, so no later than 20:50. Please confirm the hydrant and who meets the drivers.

(2) The quarantine order goes out by 11:50. I still have ONE access point listed (CR 12 main drive). Is the 230th Street field lane in or out?

Thank you,
Quarantine Officer, IP-1
Minnesota Board of Animal Health
fields.signature:
Pete Vasquez
County Highway Engineer
Calder County Highway Department | 555-0140

instructorNote: This tests whether the EOC gives the Board both IP-1 access points before the 11:50 quarantine order and makes the 230th Street lane a staffed or barricaded control under Board authority, not a county closure. Check whether OPS confirms the west lot and its hydrant, names someone to meet the trailers, and notices that Saturday's 60-vendor swap meet at the fairgrounds clashes with staging. The Sheriff is still short of deputies, so watch for him trading a checkpoint for the gate.
